commitResults.messageTitle: README: Update references from Duke to Lune
commitResults.messageBody:
The project and class were renamed from Duke to Lune earlier, but the
README/docs/README instructions and sample output still referenced the
old name and banner text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add present-changes-visually and test-ui Claude Code skills, plus a UI test plan
commitResults.messageBody:
present-changes-visually (adapted from se-edu/skill-present-changes-visually)
generates a self-contained HTML side-by-side diff for reviewing changes.

test-ui runs the console test cases recorded in test/ui-test-plan.md against
the compiled program, comparing actual output to expected output per case,
and stopping immediately with an expected-vs-actual report on the first
failure. test/ui-test-plan.md currently has 14 cases covering the greet/exit,
todo/deadline/event, mark/unmark/delete, and error-handling behavior added so
far, including several that specifically interleave valid and invalid input
to catch bugs that only corrupt internal state (task numbering, done status)
rather than crashing outright.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle more edge cases and errors
Extract TaskList class to hold the task list
commitResults.messageBody:
Working toward the Ui/Storage/Parser/TaskList decomposition target,
starting with TaskList since it's the lowest-risk extraction: a pure
data wrapper around the existing ArrayList<Task>, with no dependency
on how errors get printed (unlike Storage) or how parsing/execution
get split (unlike Parser/Ui). It implements Iterable<Task> so callers
never need to reach into the underlying ArrayList directly.

Lune.java now holds a TaskList instead of an ArrayList<Task> directly;
processCommand() and saveTasks() take a TaskList parameter. Since
TaskList exposes the same method names (add/remove/get/size) plus
Iterable, the call sites inside processCommand needed no changes.
loadTasks() still returns ArrayList<Task> for now, wrapped into a
TaskList at the call site in main() — aligning it with a Storage class
is next iteration's job, not this one.

No behavior change: all 24 cases in test/ui-test-plan.md still pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: build.gradle: Fix mainClass and jar name after merging Gradle support
commitResults.messageBody:
The add-gradle-support branch was created before the Duke->Lune rename
and the later package reorganization, so mainClass still pointed at
seedu.duke.Duke, which no longer exists. Updated to lune.Lune (the
actual entry point post-reorg), and renamed the shadowJar output from
duke.jar to lune.jar to match.

Verified: ./gradlew build succeeds, and ./gradlew run correctly starts
the chatbot.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests and apply SE-EDU style fixes
commitResults.messageBody:
Per the project's 50% coverage target, the codebase's highest-value
logic -- command dispatch, date/time parsing, save-file validation,
and date-range matching -- had no unit-level tests, only end-to-end
console coverage via the test-ui skill. Separately, an audit against
the newly-mandated SE-EDU coding standard found a few concrete
violations in the same files.

Let's:
* add EventTest/DeadlineTest for occursOn/toString/toSaveFormat, and
  LuneTest for CommandType.fromInput, parseTaskIndex, parseDateTime,
  parseSavedTask, and parseSavedDateTime -- widening those from
  private to package-private to make them testable
* reorder Lune.java's imports so this project's own lune.* imports
  come after java.*, per the standard's required group ordering
* add the required "// Fallthrough" comment where case UNKNOWN
  intentionally falls through to default
* reword each occursOn() Javadoc summary to start with a verb
  ("Returns whether ..."), since "Whether ..." isn't one

Deliberately not covered by tests: TaskList's one-line delegates,
Todo's two-line overrides, and Task's plain getters/setters, since
they're lower value than the logic above.

The project has no stated policy on how much of the codebase JUnit
should cover, or when to update tests as code changes.

Let's document the agreed target: JUnit tests should cover the top
~50% highest-value methods (complex/core/critical logic), and must
be kept up to date after any code change so coverage doesn't
silently drift below that target as the codebase grows.

commitResults.messageTitle: test-ui skill: adapt to package layout
commitResults.messageBody:
Source moved from a flat src/main/java into package subdirectories
(lune/, lune/task/, lune/exception/) as part of the A-Packages
increment. The skill's compile step used a non-recursive glob, so
it would find zero source files under the new layout, and its
default --main-class no longer matched the fully-qualified class
name.

Let's:
* switch the compile step from glob("*.java") to rglob("*.java") so
  it finds source under any package subdirectory
* update the --main-class default, and the SKILL.md examples, from
  Lune to lune.Lune

commitResults.messageTitle: Add and mandate SE-EDU Java coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
The project had no documented Java style convention, so style was
left to whatever felt reasonable case by case.

Let's add the seedu-java-coding-standard skill, encoding the full
SE-EDU intermediate standard (naming, layout, import order,
brace/whitespace style, Javadoc format), and mandate it in
AGENTS.md for all Java code -- new or edited, main or test -- from
now on.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add and mandate SE-EDU Git conventions
commitResults.messageBody:
The project had no documented commit-message or branch-naming
convention, so past messages varied in format.

Let's add the seedu-git-standard skill, encoding the full SE-EDU
Git conventions (imperative-mood subject line, 50/72-char limits,
what/why-not-how body, kebab-case branch names), and mandate it in
AGENTS.md for every future commit and branch name. This governs how
a commit is written, not whether to make one -- the existing rule
against committing without explicit permission is unchanged.
